text: Almost a year since I last sent this message. 11 months and 14 days to be exact. While I'm not calling a bottom, the level of sustained bid at 60k was impressive. We can trade down to 74k and I'd still be very bullish, enter low 70s/high 60s and it would be time to reconsider. This past week we've had the main utility runners on RH do 3-5x and only seen the small caps really take off in the past few days. Betas to AI and Pons/Uni have still been pushing into 8 fig mcap which is great to see and a luxury we haven't had for a long time. Strength of betas is a good resemblance of how much froth/strength is in the market. While it's easy to feel the fomo of missing the runners, if this is the turning point for onchain there will be so many opportunities. Because we've had such shit conditions for the past year, having multiple 9 fig runners feels over stimulating. Turn back to AI szn and we didn't really get started until ai16z was at 500 mil and it still did a 4x from there while the entire eco repriced significantly higher as well. Thankfully we have majors on our side and only 30% off the lows. While it's important to significantly ramp up screen time, remember this bull market will be a marathon and not a sprint. Don't burn yourself out because you didn't catch the two vertical coins when it's still a mine field playing new pairs, despite significantly better volume. Surviving this bull is just as much of a physical battle as a mental battle. Yes you can run on the euphoria of potential PNL and hunger, eventually you'll reach a tipping point on week four where you've averaged three hours sleep every night. That decay in health eventually carries over to your trading framework, most importantly your risk management. It took me a long time to realize this, at the same time you need to walk the line of simply outworking everyone. We each have our own capacity outputs and mental limitations. The times I get most frustrated with myself is when im not reaching my maximum potential, as I know when I'm in my flow state I feel like I'm untouchable and can produce work that feels supernatural to when I'm in a more passive state. Which is why I have such a regimented protocol for when I'm trying to up my read on the market as it's a personal battle with understanding your own psyche and limitations you've set on yourself. As you take more action those limitations can slowly be removed, the biggest focus is keeping to your risk management while your limitations are removed as growing PNL can easily cause over confidence. Especially in these conditions, over confidence is the last thing you want with how infrequent good spots appear and how frequent rotations are. Reminder that it's only been 64 days since ansem coin took off and we're still deep in the bear market. Time is on our side and there will be a meta at some point for most trading styles, we shift through them rather fast, just matters how much attention you pay. The past 24 hours is the first reasonable pullback we've seen and signs of froth slowing down. In my last twitter post I said how we're approaching the end of wave two for the RH eco, especially if there's no listing for one of the main utility coins. First reaction is that it plays out similar to Cashcat, the RH team wait for the blow off top then assess which teams are the best positioned to carry out their narrative of tokenized stocks and other onchain agendas to push more native users into their eco. Onchain is still in a great position, we were due for a flush and the coming few days will be very important to assess strength and demand for leading coins to determine how the next leg looks. Typically Sunday flush with a correction after 2-3 weeks of up only.

text: PONS has done $46.1M in launchpad fees so far, but the important distinction is that not all of those fees are buying PONS. Over the last 24 hours, the platform did $5.34M in fees, while $22.8k actually went towards buying and burning PONS, around 0.43% of total fees ($22.8k of buy pressure on around $8m of on-chain liquidity is a ~1% price movement). The reason is pretty simple, V1 uses roughly 80% of its protocol revenue to buy and burn PONS, while V2 doesn't. V2 keeps its protocol share in the paired asset, and if a creator enables buybacks, those buybacks go into the launched meme token instead. V2 now accounts for around 87% of fees over the last week. So the launchpad numbers are genuinely large, $46.1M in lifetime fees, $10.1M in protocol revenue, $3.61M of actual PONS buybacks, but as volume has shifted towards V2, the direct relationship between launchpad fees and PONS buy pressure has become much weaker. Worth understanding if you're looking at PONS primarily through the buyback thesis.

text: Russia's Regulated Crypto Trading Volume Expected to Exceed $46 Billion in First Year According to Bitcoin News, Sberbank Deputy Chairman Anatoly Popov said regulated Russian exchanges are expected to record at least $46.43 billion in crypto trading volume during the first year, potentially rising to $87.06 billion by 2029. Russia's central bank plans to allow investors to legally purchase crypto assets through brokers starting September 1. Non-qualified investors will be limited to purchasing up to $3,800 worth of crypto assets annually through a single licensed intermediary. Official exchanges are currently authorized to trade only Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Tether. — link

text: Highlight Clip: Arthur Hayes: How the 2008 Bailout Gave Birth to Bitcoin Arthur Hayes: How the 2008 Bailout Gave Birth to Bitcoin In an August 23, 2026 video interview with Altcoin Daily, BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes recalled that in the 2008 crisis, Washington didn't bail out Bear Stearns directly — it had JP Morgan buy the bank for $2 backed by massive loans, a sweetheart deal for JP Morgan. Lehman then failed, and regulators found they didn't really like free markets after all. Major bank CEOs trekked to Washington and walked away with roughly $700 billion in taxpayer money, while Goldman bankers kept their bonuses and ordinary people lost their homes. He argues the U.S. broke its promise of sound money in the bailout — and Bitcoin was born as a response to that broken trust. — link
